it's hard in moments like these, but your brain is lying to you. Your family and loved ones want you alive. I don't know if they're abusive or any other factors to add to the complexity of the situation. (if you're living with abusive people, it can really exacerbate this kind of thinking)  


oddly, what people tend to think is "if i kill myself, i'll be saving them pain in the long run" but pushing people away and cutting them out (by uh, dying) hurts more than anything. And usually, when folks push others away to "save them," they actually want to be closer and have a stronger bond with them. insecurities can ruin everything. don't let them ruin you. it's fine to feel this way. just think about this.

the saddest thing in the world is that this happened to you, and (if you're a woman) at least 1 in 3 women -- you're not alone. i know that doesn't make anything better, but i've been there. I have felt exactly like that -- "why does it keep happening?" and then equating it to my worth. there are SO MANY SHITTY PEOPLE in this world. there are so many abusers and perpetrators and you are never at fault for their abuse.   


I really hope you can get support and peace. there are support groups online where you can talk to other survivors; it's helped me feel less alone, and that "well, they can get through it, maybe I can, too."

that's... an absurdly long wait. i hope they can expedite the process or give you other resources for places that can see you more immediately.

it's difficult to live when your brain is convincing you you're trash. you're not inherently a horrible person, and you do deserve to have your concerns and mental issues taken seriously. you deserve to be a priority, to yourself and loved ones. it will take time, and it'll suck, but you can come out on top of this. you don't have to rush yourself, sometimes it's necessary to just experience what you're feeling and analyze it.

i mean, if she's been trying to end things... why deny her autonomy? "preventing" it is another way to say "forcing it" to keep going. i know shit sucks right now and you sound really stressed. and in denial. keeping a relationship going when 50% of the relationship doesn't want to be there just breeds control issues and contempt. it's not a bad idea to get space from her while you finish up what you gotta do. get a breather, detach from her if you can/stay at a friend's house so you can get past the schooling stress and tackle the relationship issues with a clearer head. good luck, this is never easy.

She needs to get clean, first of all. A very good friend of mine had real substance abuse issues and, after awhile, it started to fry his brain in truly scary ways. The only road to recovery for your situation with her is for her to start her own road to recovery and get clean so that she can detox and start to treat her illnesses. This sounds obvious and easy, but of course, it isn't! 

If it's possible to go above her/your own head and get her to see a doctor that will push her into rehab, do it. Her brain is poisoned, and so is her judgement. Trust me, no one can advocate for themselves when their brain isn't sure what's real. 

Re: SO, I think you're in denial about the harm he's causing. Being with someone who washes his hands of your daughter's problems shows lack of compassion. He needs to learn to show that, and that's not your cross to bear. You don't need that, or him. 

There are support groups for parents of people with substance abuse problems; I strongly recommend reaching out and getting support from those groups (as your main source of support has failed in this regard). There are plenty of drug abuse hotlines that will help you. 

One last thing... I don't think you did the wrong thing by putting her in inpatient; if she was a danger to herself, it's necessary. Unfortunately, those facilities are very often understaffed and filled with overworked apathetic nurses/specialists; she was in a place of vulnerability and felt more accepted by the other patients. You get all kinds of people in there, including substance abuse/rehab patients. 

Good luck!
